THE fusion KPI: worldwide average household (residential) retail electricity price, population-weighted, in constant 2025 US$ per MWh. Computed by collectors/fusion.py: population-weighted mean of the GlobalPetrolPrices (GPP) per-country household prices for one GPP data quarter (final retail price incl. distribution, taxes and fees, at each country's average household consumption; USD at market exchange rates as published by GPP, i.e. converted at the rate current when GPP renders the page, hence the earliest capture; USD/kWh x 1000), over the countries GPP covers in that quarter (~100-150 countries; the note gives n and the % of world population covered), weighted by World Bank SP.POP.TOTL of the latest year <= the obs year; deflated to constant 2025 US dollars with the BLS CPI-U annual average (all items, US city average, not seasonally adjusted, series CUUR0000SA0, period M13): value x CPI2025 / CPI(obs year) (while the obs-year annual average is unpublished, the latest available year stands in and the note says so; the row is revised when it arrives). Population and CPI are as retrieved on the run date (stated in the note), not as of the capture date. Country prices come from the earliest capture stating that quarter of GPP's electricity_prices chart (to 2024) or household price world map: a Wayback Machine capture (month-sampled CDX index; published = capture date) or, for a quarter not yet archived, the first live copy we saw (published = first seen); obs = GPP data quarter (YYYY-Qn). Uncovered countries are excluded, not imputed; truncated captures are skipped; country prices above 1 USD/kWh (GPP currency-conversion errors, e.g. Syria 2.22 in 2025-Q2) and documented GPP errata (collector GPP_ERRATA) are excluded and listed in the note
